description: Frame multi-site stabilization as a submodular maximization problem under cardinality constraints. If the marginal stability gain of adding a mutation decreases as more mutations are already present (diminishing returns), the greedy algorithm provides a (1-1/e)-approximation guarantee.
mathematical_formalization: Let V = set of all candidate single mutations, k = budget. Define f(S) = predicted stability improvement of set S. If f is monotone submodular, greedy achieves f(S_greedy) >= (1 - 1/e) * f(S_optimal). Total cost: O(k * |V|) scorer evaluations.
analogical_connections: Sensor placement: placing sensors to maximize information coverage is submodular
Feature selection in ML: selecting features for maximum mutual information is submodular
Sviridenko (2004) showed (1-1/e)-approximation is tight for cardinality constraints
implementation_hypothesis: Pre-screen N=50-100 candidate single mutations from ESM-2. Define f(S) = ESM-2 pseudo-likelihood. Test submodularity empirically. Run greedy with lazy evaluation. Expected O(k*N) calls with lazy eval.
experiment_seed: For 30 proteins, enumerate subsets of size 2-4 from top-20 single mutants. Check submodularity ratio. Compare greedy vs exhaustive search.
